## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.0-beta.2 extends reviewed topic updates to private Obsidian evidence and lets you explicitly add supported one-hop code dependencies or configuration files.

### Review private note updates

An existing private memory backed by one Obsidian note can now join the experimental topic maintenance workflow. When the note changes, you select and retain the supporting excerpt, review the proposed update in Manager, and separately approve the exact full document before it is saved. The original evidence and protected policy and history stay visible through the review.

Manager makes these proposals easier to inspect with clearer status badges, quoted evidence, and focused comparisons between accepted and proposed text. Source access or evidence problems remain visible and block acceptance.

### Choose additional dependencies

For a private code-backed topic, you can review a bounded one-hop neighborhood and choose the exact code sources to add. Configuration files are separate explicit selections. Threadnote shows the complete unchanged topic and the selected additions before you approve the new dependency scope.

This remains an opt-in beta workflow with human review at every write. Threadnote does not accept proposals or expand evidence scope automatically. Usefulness, review effort, and general answer quality have not yet been established.
